hook.line: Tomás has to call the taller about the car, and a polite voice picks up. In Colombia you don't ask whether someone is there: you ask to be put through, and you use *usted*.
hook.en: Could you put me through to Mrs Gómez? (formal)

rule:
Spanish doesn't ask whether someone *is there*. It asks to be connected: *¿Me comunica con…?*, always with *usted*. The person goes after *con*.

The receptionist answers *Ya lo comunico* to a man or *Ya la comunico* to a woman. Here *lo* and *la* mean "you", never *le*.

If the person is busy: *En este momento no lo puede atender* (or *la*).

Spain says *¿me pone con…?*. You will recognise it, but in Colombia use *comunicar*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *lo* and *la* here direct object pronouns: they stand for the person being connected.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *comunica* or *comunico*: ¿Me ___ con la señora Gómez? Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: You are asking the other person, who is *usted*, so *comunica*.

yourTurn.prompt: You are the receptionist, talking to a woman. Choose *lo* or *la*: Ya ___ comunico con el taller. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Ya la comunico con el taller.
yourTurn.why: *La* stands for the woman you are connecting.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, formal: Could you put me through to Vale, please?
yourTurn.why: *Comunicar con* is the frame, with *usted* and *me* for yourself.

yourTurn.prompt: You are the receptionist. Tell the man on the line you are putting him through now.
yourTurn.why: *Lo* is the man you are connecting, and the present tense works for "now".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: She can't take your call right now. (to a man)
yourTurn.answer: En este momento no lo puede atender.
yourTurn.why: *Lo* is the man calling, and *no puede atender* means she can't see to him.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it friendly (*tú*): *¿Me comunica con Vale?*
yourTurn.why: A friend is *tú*, so the verb ends in *-s*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask, formal, to be put through to the garage.
accept: ¿Me comunica con el taller, por favor?
yourTurn.why: The place or person goes after *con*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Connecting someone is always *comunicar con*, never *a*.

pitfalls.wrong: Ya le comunico con el doctor.
pitfalls.right: Ya lo comunico con el doctor.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Here *lo* (to a man) and *la* (to a woman) stand for the person you connect.
Almost. On a call to people you don't know, use *usted*: *comunica*, not *comunicas*.

personal: Imagine you are calling a clinic or an office. Ask to be put through to someone: *¿Me comunica con…?*
